equity_bridge.item: Cox Equity Holdings convertible preferred units of Charter Holdings (liquidation preference)
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q Note 9: 60M units, $6.0B face, 6.875% cash dividend (~$412M/yr), conversion price $477.41 (deep out of the money at the current price) -> treated as a fixed claim at par.

equity_bridge.item: Charter Series A preferred stock issued in the Liberty Broadband Transaction
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q Note 3: mandatorily redeemable 2039, fair value $159M recorded in other long-term liabilities.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+17.8% 3yr, -7.5% 5yr) is meaningless as a growth proxy: book equity is driven by ~$80B of cumulative debt-funded buybacks since 2016, not by retained value. EPS CAGR (+18.4% 5yr) is buyback-driven share shrink (209M -> 138M shares FY2020-25) on flat-to-slightly-rising net income; the EPS column is basic EPS (known XBRL bug). Revenue (0.5% 3yr) is the honest organic growth rate and is used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = CSV FCF (OCF - capex) less SBC: FY2020 $6,796M, FY2022 $5,079M, FY2025 $3,745M. Owner-FCF CAGR (-9.7% 3yr) is below reported (-7.3%) because SBC grew from $351M to $673M while FCF fell -- the decline is mostly the capex cycle (network evolution + rural build lifted capex from $7.4B to $11.7B, 15% -> 21% of revenue), not SBC. FY2025-FY2020 CAGRs measured on legacy Charter only (pre-Cox).

scenario_narratives.base: Charter's four axes are broadband share against fixed-wireless (T-Mobile/Verizon/AT&T) and fibre overbuild, Cox integration and the $3B savings programme, the capex cliff as network evolution and the RDOF/rural build finish, and a balance sheet at 3.9x net debt/EBITDA. Base: pro forma revenue keeps shrinking for three years (-1.5% to 0%: Internet customers still falling ~150k/quarter legacy, video and voice in structural decline, mobile lines +1.6M/yr partly offsetting) then grows ~1% as converged bundles and pricing hold; Adjusted EBITDA margin rises from ~40.3% to 43% on ~$2B of the $3B targeted run-rate savings (the rest reinvested in promotions and service); capex falls from ~$14B to ~17% of revenue; cash tax ramps from a bonus-depreciation-depressed 16% to 21%. Deleveraging to the 3.5x target absorbs most of the FCF for three years.
scenario_narratives.bull: The new operating model works: simpler, transparent pricing plus mobile layering cut churn and Charter returns to Internet customer growth across a 70M-passing footprint by 2028; the full $3B of savings is retained, taking margin to 44.5%; capex reverts to ~15.5% of revenue once the upgrade cycle ends; revenue compounds ~2% and the equity re-rates as leverage falls through 3.5x. Leverage works for the shareholder: each $1B of EV is ~$6/share.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Altice-USA path at a slower pace: FWA and fibre take another 15-20% of broadband share over the decade, pricing pressure eats the synergies, margin slides to 38% and revenue declines 1.5-2.5% a year in perpetuity, while capex cannot fall because a second upgrade (fibre-deep/DOCSIS 4.0) is needed to compete. With ~$113B of debt and preferred ahead of the common, this path leaves the equity with little or no value -- the bear outcome is a solvency-of-equity question, not a multiple question.
scenario_narratives.integration_note: Cox closed 2026-08-19; preliminary purchase accounting; Q3-2026 consolidated only ~6 weeks of Cox. Synergy and savings targets are management's and unproven.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on a Cox-pro-forma base, with all fixed claims (debt at carrying value, Cox convertible preferred at par, Liberty preferred) deducted and the A/N and Cox Holdings common units counted as Class A equivalents. The equity is a thin, highly levered residual; the scenario spread is wide by construction and the bear weight is raised accordingly rather than adding a WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: Broadband share loss to fixed-wireless and fibre overbuild accelerates (legacy Internet customers -156k in Q3-2026)
Cox integration and the $3B savings programme under-deliver or are competed away in price
Capex fails to fall as network evolution ends because a further upgrade cycle is required
Refinancing risk on $108.6B of principal at 6-8% new-issue coupons; leverage 3.93x vs 3.5x target
Equity is ~13% of EV at the current price: every $1B of EV is ~$6/share, so small driver changes move IV by large percentages
Preliminary Cox purchase accounting; tax receivable agreement pays A/N and Cox 50% of exchange step-up benefits

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 101.11-254.11
data_sources.financials: CHTR_Metrics.csv (XBRL), FY2023-FY2025 10-Ks and Q3-2026 10-Q (balance sheet, Cox purchase-price note, NCI note 9, EPS note 14, pro forma revenue, liquidity section)
data_sources.qualitative: Q3-2026 10-Q MD&A (new operating model, $1B Cox synergies + $2B additional savings, 3.5x leverage target); CHTR_Analysis.json was not yet available at build time

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement 'Stock compensation expense' $673M (CHTR_Annual_FY2025.txt:3018); 9M-2026 $518M (Q3-2026 10-Q). Charter publishes no combined SBC+withholding-tax figure; net-share-settlement withholding sits in financing 'Other, net' and is not separately disclosed, so the add-back alone is used (understates the cost slightly).
inputs.fy0: TTM Sep-2026 pro forma (Charter + Cox Communications)
inputs.share_count_basis: As-exchanged economic count, Q3-2026 10-Q: 114.454M Class A outstanding (cover) + ~15.5M Charter Holdings common units held by A/N (EPS note, 15,511,283 weighted, no 2026 purchases) + 33.6M Charter Holdings common units issued to Cox Equity Holdings (exchangeable 1:1 into Class A) + ~1.0M dilutive equity awards (treasury method at a depressed price; 1.2M in the 9M-2026 diluted count). The Cox convertible preferred units (60M units, $6.0B liquidation preference, 6.875% cash dividend, convertible into ~12.6M common units at $477.41) are deep out of the money and are deducted at liquidation preference in the equity bridge instead of being added to the count. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 7.0% USD WACC, same in every scenario (risk charged once, in the scenario flows and weights). Market-value capital structure is ~85% debt / ~15% equity at the current price: after-tax cost of debt ~4.9% (2026 issues priced 6.05-7.85% pre-tax, x(1-21%)), cost of equity ~13-14% for an equity sliver levered ~5.5x (US 10y ~4.3% + levered beta ~1.6 x 5.5% ERP), arithmetic ~6.2-6.5%. Rounded UP to 7.0% because the arithmetic WACC falls as leverage rises, which would reward the very balance-sheet risk that is the bear axis; 7% is also the conventional unlevered rate for US cable.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), naturally: Charter reports under US GAAP, so operating lease cost is already inside operating expenses and Adjusted EBITDA; operating lease liabilities (~$1.4B) are excluded from net debt. Finance leases assumed with Cox are immaterial and sit inside the debt carrying value.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged ONCE via the share count: the flows are consolidated Charter Holdings flows (100%), and the A/N and Cox Charter Holdings common units are added to the divisor as Class A equivalents (exchangeable 1:1), so no NCI stock is deducted in the bridge. The Cox convertible preferred is a fixed claim and is deducted at its $6.0B liquidation preference in equity_bridge (its 6.875% dividend is therefore NOT also deducted from the flows). Calibration: consolidated FY2025 net income $5,766M = attributable $4,987M + NCI $779M (A/N ~11%); on the as-exchanged basis the per-unit earnings are the same whichever way it is cut. Cash tax is applied to 100% of EBIT, which is mildly conservative: Charter Holdings is a partnership and A/N/Cox bear tax on their share at the partner level (paid via Holdings tax distributions), economically equivalent to a full corporate charge on exchanged units.
inputs.debt_note: total_debt is the 2026-09-30 carrying value of long-term debt: $1,990M current + $105,062M non-current = $107,052M. Principal outstanding is $108.6B ($13.7B credit facilities, $68.2B IG secured notes, $26.7B HY unsecured); the ~$1.5B gap is the fair-value discount on assumed Cox debt and on the August 2026 exchange notes, i.e. the debt's economic value. The $1,696M EIP (equipment installment plan) financing facility is EXCLUDED from net debt because it is matched by EIP receivables of at least that amount (self-liquidating device financing); including one requires including the other.
inputs.pro_forma_note: base_revenue $66,400M = pro forma 9M-2026 revenue $49,720M (Q3-2026 10-Q Selected Pro Forma, line 1710) + an estimated pro forma Q4-2025 of ~$16.7B (legacy Q4-2025 $13,601M + Cox ~$3.1B; consistent with the pro forma Q3-2025 $16,764M). Pro forma revenue is shrinking ~1.5-1.8% YoY (Q3 -1.5%, 9M -1.8%). Pro forma Adjusted EBITDA margin ~40.3% (legacy Q2-2026 40.3%, Q3-2026 consolidated 39.8% inclusive of Cox transition expenses).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route), scenario-weighted -- Charter is a US operating company (cable broadband, mobile, video), not a bank/REIT/holdco; first valuation of this ticker so no prior model to match. The extreme capital structure is handled in the bridge, not the flows: unlevered owner FCF is discounted at a 7% WACC and $106.5B net debt plus $6.2B of preferred claims is deducted, leaving a thin equity residual (~13% of EV at market) whose value moves ~$1.6/share for every $1B (0.75%) of EV. Read the IV spread with that leverage in mind. The base year is TTM Sep-2026 PRO FORMA for Cox (closed 2026-08-19) because the reported FY2025 base excludes ~$13B of revenue and the post-close balance sheet already carries Cox's $10.2B of debt; mixing a legacy revenue base with a post-close balance sheet would understate value by ~20% of EV. The Q3-2026 net loss (-$2,397M attributable) is non-recurring -- $6.3B franchise impairment, $1.4-1.6B gain on debt extinguishment, Cox transaction costs -- and is not used anywhere. last_fcf $4,331M is FY2025 legacy LEVERED owner FCF (company FCF $5,004M incl. a +$586M accrued-capex timing benefit, less SBC $673M); the projection itself is unlevered and built from components. Buybacks ($5.1B FY2025, $1.9B 9M-2026) are debt-funded at a ~3.5-4.5x leverage target; they are value-neutral here and, with leverage now 3.93x against a 3.5x target within three years, management says debt paydown takes priority. Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes $893M were depressed by OBBBA's restored 100% bonus depreciation; unlevered-equivalent rate on EBIT ~16% (cash taxes + interest shield), ramped to 21%.

bear.narrative: Fixed-wireless and fibre overbuilders keep taking broadband share; the savings are spent on price and promotions and margin drifts to 38%; capex stays elevated near 19% because the network has to be upgraded again to compete; the business is in managed decline.

base.narrative: Cox integration lands about two-thirds of the $3B of targeted run-rate savings ($1B Cox synergies + $2B operating-model savings); broadband net losses slow as the new go-to-market and mobile bundling take hold; capex falls from ~21.5% to 17% of revenue as network evolution and the subsidised rural build complete.

bull.narrative: Full $3B of savings realised and largely retained; converged broadband+mobile bundles return the combined footprint to customer growth by 2028; capex settles near the pre-cycle 15-16% of revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% (from the 15% house default) because legacy Internet customers are still declining every quarter, the Cox integration and the new operating model are both unproven, and ~87% of EV is senior to the common so modest operating misses wipe out disproportionate equity value. Base held at 50%: synergy and capex-decline paths are management-guided and mechanically likely. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- return to customer growth, full savings retention, and capex normalising to pre-cycle levels.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
